title: Determinism drift hunt
summary: Widens the determinism fingerprint one unpinned field at a time and fixes every cross-process divergence it exposes, never by loosening the pin.
seoTitle: Determinism Drift Hunt | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Extends the architecture fingerprint by construction so an unpinned engine field cannot hide a cross-process divergence, then repairs the engine rather than the assertion.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Pick one determinism surface in FootballSimCore that no current assertion pins: a store, ledger, scheduler or calendar field absent from the pinned fingerprints. Extend the --architecture-only suite to pin it by construction, then run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane determinism in two separate process invocations and compare. Fix any divergence in the engine, never by loosening a pin or re-recording a literal to match. Record each widening in docs/STATUS.md. Stop when two consecutive passes add coverage and find no divergence. Ask before changing an existing pinned fingerprint literal.
verifyTitle: Two separate process invocations of the widened determinism lane produce identical fingerprints.
verifyDetail: Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane determinism twice as distinct processes on the same commit and seed, and compare the recorded root and one-week transition fingerprints byte for byte. The widened assertion must enumerate its field set by construction, so a field added later is covered the day it is added. A pass that only re-runs the existing pins is not evidence; the acceptance check is the widened pin holding, not the old one still passing.
useWhen: Use when the seeding contract in docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 3 must hold against fields no assertion currently reaches, or after any change to GameState entity stores, the WorldScheduler, the domain-event ledger or seed derivation. The prior build seeded from UUID.hashValue, which is salted per launch, so one save produced a different league every app start and no in-process test could see it; that class of fault is invisible until the fingerprint reaches the field.
steps: List the fields the current --architecture-only fingerprints actually cover, and the engine state they do not reach.
Choose the single unpinned field with the widest blast radius across the 15-step WorldScheduler.
Extend the assertion to enumerate its class by construction rather than by hand-listing instances.
Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane determinism as two separate process invocations and diff the fingerprints.
If they diverge, fix the engine. Never widen, delete or re-record the pin to make it green.
Re-run both invocations and confirm the widened pin holds.
Record the widening and its result in docs/STATUS.md, naming the files touched.
Repeat with the next unpinned field; stop after two consecutive clean widenings.
why: Running the existing determinism suite only re-detects faults the suite already knows how to see. An unknown determinism fault lives outside the current coverage boundary by definition, so the only pass that can find one is a pass that moves the boundary first. This is the project's own stated convention: the coverage boundary must not become the quality boundary, and a test that checks a class must enumerate that class by construction. Fixing a divergence by re-recording the expected literal converts a real fault into a permanently green lie, which is why the loop forbids it explicitly rather than trusting judgement.
note: Cross-process determinism cannot be proven inside one process. If the environment has no Swift toolchain, this loop stops as blocked; write the assertion anyway to the same standard and record it in docs/STATUS.md as unverified and never compiled, per CLAUDE.md. Never report a written-but-uncompiled assertion as a passing gate.

title: World generation invariant widening
summary: Adds one generation invariant per pass across programmes, conferences, rosters and identities, and repairs the generator wherever a wider seed sweep breaks it.
seoTitle: World Generation Invariant Widening | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Sweeps generated worlds at many seeds against invariants the current suite does not assert, so a generator fault that only appears at an untried seed is found before a player finds it.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Name one property of a generated world that docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11 requires and no suite asserts: conference sizes summing to 134, division shape, roster position templates, trait distribution, jersey-number legality or rating spread. Assert it across a seed sweep, then run the --generation-only and --trait-population suites. Identity distribution has no flag of its own and is reached only by the default full run, so use that lane when the property touches names or identity. Fix the generator, not the invariant. Stop when two consecutive passes add an invariant and find no failure. Escalate any fix that would change a documented rules constant.
verifyTitle: The new invariant holds across the full seed sweep with the generator unchanged in shape.
verifyDetail: Run the generation suites over a seed sweep no smaller than the 200 leagues docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11.3.5 already uses for the legal tests, so one generation run serves both. Note that runIdentityDistributionTests is dispatched only from the default no-flag run, so a property touching names or identity is not covered by --generation-only alone. The invariant must be expressed against the rules module rather than a copied literal, so a change to the rules constant moves the assertion with it. A single-seed pass is not evidence: generation faults are seed-conditional by nature, and the seed that exposes one is exactly the seed nobody tried.
useWhen: Use when generated worlds must satisfy a documented structural or distributional property that no current assertion reaches, or after any change under Sources/FootballSimCore/Generation. Conference composition is generated per league rather than listed, so the shape is the only thing a test can hold; that makes the shape assertions the whole of the safety net.
steps: Read docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11 and list the structural and distributional properties it fixes.
Diff that list against what the generation suites actually assert.
Pick the unasserted property whose violation would be least visible to a player and most damaging to the league.
Express it against the rules module constants, not against copied literals.
Run it across a seed sweep of at least 200 leagues, using the default full run when identity is in scope.
Repair the generator where the sweep fails; never relax the invariant to fit the generator.
Confirm the retry budget still terminates: a generator that can loop forever is a hang, not a fix.
Record the widening in docs/STATUS.md and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: A generated world is the one artefact in this project that no author reviews before a player sees it. Every other surface passes through a human; a league at seed 41,988 does not. That makes generation the aspect where the gap between what is asserted and what is true is widest, and where an unknown fault survives longest. Sweeping many seeds against one new invariant per pass converts that open-ended risk into a bounded, repeatable search whose progress is measurable: either the sweep found something or the boundary moved and it did not.
note: A generated-name or colour finding is a legal matter, not a generation bug. Hand it to the legal partition sweep rather than fixing it here, and never resolve a borderline identity question inside this loop; CLAUDE.md requires it go to the owner and to counsel.

title: Legal partition sweep
summary: Holds the name-collision and trade-dress tests to a strict partition of every generated name, so a name kind that neither sweep checks cannot exist.
seoTitle: Legal Partition Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Audits the two legal tests for names and colour pairs that fall between their coverage, extends the partition assertion, and escalates every identity question rather than resolving it.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Enumerate every kind of name a generated world produces and check that each is swept by either the institution-kind check or the place-kind check, never neither. Extend the partition assertion by construction, then run the --legal-only suite across at least 200 leagues along with the trade-dress delta-E check on both members of each colour pair in both orientations. Fix generation, never the threshold. Stop when two consecutive passes add coverage and find nothing. Escalate every borderline identity to the owner; resolve none yourself.
verifyTitle: Every generated name is swept by exactly one limb, and no colour pair falls inside delta-E 25 on both members.
verifyDetail: Run --legal-only across at least 200 generated leagues, matching the sample docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11.3.5 fixes. The partition assertion must fail if a name kind is added that neither Blocklist.blocks nor Blocklist.blocksPlaceName is asked about, because a name that belongs to neither kind is a name nothing checks. Trade dress is CIE L*a*b* CIE76 delta-E 25 on both primary and secondary, checked in both orientations, since swapping the pair does not make it original.
useWhen: Use before any release, after any change to the name banks, the blocklist, the colour generator or the set of named entity kinds, and whenever a new kind of generated name is introduced. This is the guardrail CLAUDE.md calls absolute, and college identity, trade dress and player NIL are among the most aggressively enforced intellectual property in sport.
steps: Enumerate every named entity kind a generated world produces, from the generator rather than from memory.
Map each kind to the institution-kind limb or the place-kind limb and find the ones mapped to neither.
Extend the partition assertion so an unmapped kind fails the suite by construction.
Run --legal-only across at least 200 leagues and record collisions with the seed that produced them.
Fix the generator or the name bank. Never raise the delta-E threshold or trim the blocklist to pass.
Confirm the deterministic fallback pair still satisfies both tests and the contrast floors.
Collect anything borderline into one list for the owner and counsel, and stop rather than deciding it.
Record the sweep and its sample size in docs/STATUS.md; repeat until two consecutive passes are clean.
why: The blocklist is a denylist, not a definition of compliance, and the project already records the gap: a programme whose ratings, conference, geography and history are individually fictional but jointly identify a real one is trade-dress adjacent and no test in the package covers it. That is precisely why the mechanical part must be airtight. The partition is the load-bearing idea, because the failure it prevents is not a collision the test missed but a name kind the test was never pointed at, which no amount of re-running finds.
note: Real location names are permitted for cities and regions by owner decision, but not for venues, and eight real cities are refused as institution names while permitted as the city a programme plays in. The line is what kind of name it is, not what the string says, so a fix that special-cases a string rather than a kind is the wrong fix. Never propose real-name data files, roster importers or a wink in the store listing as a route around a failure.

title: Match engine oracle widening
summary: Adds one situational oracle per pass to play resolution, the clock and the anchor contract, and repairs the engine wherever the widened oracle catches an illegal state.
seoTitle: Match Engine Oracle Widening | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Extends the match engine's assertions into situations the current suite does not construct, so an illegal down, clock, formation or anchor state is caught by a test rather than by a player.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Choose one match situation the engine can reach and the suite never constructs: a clock or down edge, a scoring-play boundary, an overtime path, or an anchor set at the field bound. Assert its legality, then run the --engine, --match-reducer and --snap-anchors suites. Fix the engine where the new oracle fails. Keep each change bounded and re-run all three. Stop when two consecutive passes add a situation and find nothing. Ask before changing any calibrated outcome distribution.
verifyTitle: The widened oracle passes with the engine repaired and no calibration band moved.
verifyDetail: Run --engine, --match-reducer and --snap-anchors after each change, then confirm ./scripts/verify.sh --lane calibration is unmoved. A legality repair that shifts a calibrated distribution is two changes, not one: the legality fix is in scope and the distribution shift must be justified against docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 5 or reverted. Anchor legality, coordinate space, alignment and bound are contract clauses in section 9 and each is separately assertable.
useWhen: Use after any change to play resolution, the clock model, the reducer or the anchor contract, and whenever a match situation is reachable in play but absent from the suite. The anchor contract added pursuit and the tackle in August 2026 and section 9.7 still names what is not drawn, so the gap between the contract and its assertions is documented rather than hypothetical.
steps: Enumerate the match situations the reducer can produce, from the state machine rather than from the tests.
Diff that against the situations the suite actually constructs.
Pick one uncovered situation and assert its legality, not its aesthetics.
Run --engine, --match-reducer and --snap-anchors.
Repair the engine where the oracle fails, in one bounded change.
Re-run the three suites, then confirm the calibration lane has not moved.
If a band did move, stop and justify it against docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 5 before continuing.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: The match engine is the one system whose faults are both most visible and least reproducible: a wrong down or an impossible formation appears once, at one seed, in one drive, and is gone. Assertions are the only durable memory of what legal means. Widening the oracle situation by situation is the only search that reaches states the current tests never build, and separating legality from calibration keeps a legality fix from quietly buying itself a distribution change nobody priced.
note: This loop asserts legality, not realism. Realism belongs to the calibration band tightening loop, which uses TOST against stated targets. Keeping them apart is what stops a plausible-looking outcome change from being justified by the test that was written to accommodate it.

title: Calibration band tightening
summary: Tightens one calibration band per pass under TOST, across the paired lane and the two-tier holdout gate, and fixes the model when a band will not hold rather than widening it.
seoTitle: Calibration Band Tightening | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Uses equivalence testing to narrow match-outcome bands one metric at a time, treating a band that will not hold as a model defect rather than a threshold to loosen.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Pick the loosest calibration band in docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 5.1 and tighten its margin one step. Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane calibration and the --m3-recruiting-calibration suite, reading the TOST confidence interval and margin rather than a point estimate. The two-tier holdout gate shares this instrument, so run --two-tier-consistency in the same pass and treat a band it derives its margin from as in scope here. If a tightening fails, fix the model or state the margin honestly in the document; never widen the band to pass, and never move a metric into the uncovered list to reach green. Stop when a band cannot be tightened without a model change you cannot justify. Ask before amending a band in canon.
verifyTitle: The tightened band holds under TOST with its confidence interval and margin recorded.
verifyDetail: The harness applies two one-sided tests and reports the confidence interval and the margin, so a passing point estimate inside a wide band is not evidence. Record the interval and the margin for the band before and after. Both tiers must hold on every metric the section lists, and the college talent-dispersion band must stay materially steeper than pro, because a top programme against a bottom one is not a coin flip.
useWhen: Use when a band is wide enough that it would pass a materially wrong model, after any change to play resolution or the abstracted model, and before any release. The prior suite carried an overtime band of 0.008 to 0.14, a seventeen-fold range, which is what widening a band to stop a false failure looks like.
steps: Rank the bands in docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 5.1 by how much wrongness each would admit.
Take the loosest and tighten its margin by one step.
Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane calibration and --m3-recruiting-calibration and read the interval, not the verdict.
If it holds, keep the tightening and record the new margin.
If it fails, diagnose the model. Fix the model or write the honest margin into canon with its reasoning.
Never widen a band to clear a failure, and never re-run at a friendlier seed to find a pass.
Amend docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md before changing the constant, per the doc-first rule.
Repeat on the next band; stop when the remaining tightening needs a model change you cannot justify.
why: A band is a claim about how wrong the simulation is allowed to be, and a wide band makes that claim vacuous. Tightening is therefore the only action that increases what the lane can detect, which makes it the only calibration action capable of finding an unknown fault. The direction of the ratchet is the whole design: a loop that may loosen has no stopping condition worth the name, because every failure has a trivially available fix that destroys the instrument.
note: Recruiting and portal model agreement is not covered by the outcome bands, which cover game outcomes only, and docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 8 names that gap. Do not report the calibration lane as evidence for recruiting-AI agreement. Amending a band is a canon change and needs the owner.

companion.prompt: Run only what this prompt names, on the commit named in the request, built with -c release. Do not widen an assertion, tighten a band, adjust a budget or fix anything: this pass reports. Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane calibration, the --m3-recruiting-calibration suite and the --two-tier-consistency gate. For every band report the TOST confidence interval and the margin, not a point estimate, and say for each whether the interval sits entirely inside the margin. Name the host. title: Season transition fuzz
summary: Walks the calendar across season boundaries at many seeds, asserting scheduling, standings, realignment and rollover invariants that the current suites do not reach.
seoTitle: Season Transition Fuzz | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Hunts the faults that only appear at a week or season boundary by advancing the world repeatedly and asserting structural legality at every transition rather than at a sampled one.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Advance the world across season boundaries at many seeds and assert one structural property the suites do not currently check at every transition: game and bye counts, standings arithmetic, conference realignment legality, rivalry ordering, or calendar step order. Run the --competition-only, --season-rollover, --realignment and --rivalry-order suites. Fix the scheduler where a transition breaks it. Stop when two consecutive passes add a property and find nothing. Ask before changing a documented calendar constant.
verifyTitle: The new property holds at every season transition across the seed sweep, not at a sampled one.
verifyDetail: Assert at every boundary the walk crosses rather than at the first and last, because boundary faults are usually conditional on a state the world only reaches after several seasons. Run --competition-only, --season-rollover, --realignment and --rivalry-order together, since a rollover repair commonly breaks scheduling and the suites are cheap enough to run as a set. Record the seed and season index of any failure so it is reproducible.
useWhen: Use after any change to the WorldScheduler, the season rollover, realignment or the shared calendar, and whenever a structural property of a season is documented in docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11.3.1 but asserted nowhere. Deterministic schedules at 134 college programmes and 32 pro teams have exact game and bye counts, so a drift is detectable but only where something looks.
steps: List the structural properties a season must satisfy from docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 11 and the rules modules.
Diff against what the competition and rollover suites assert, and where in the calendar they assert it.
Pick one property that is checked at a sampled boundary or not at all.
Assert it at every transition the walk crosses, across a seed sweep.
Run the four suites as a set and record failures with their seed and season index.
Repair the scheduler or the rollover; keep each change bounded to the failing transition.
Re-run the whole walk, not just the failing seed, so a local fix cannot hide a wider break.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: Boundaries are where state machines fail, and a season rollover is the largest boundary this world has: rosters turn over, eligibility advances, contracts expire, conferences move and the calendar resets, all in one step. A fault there is invisible in week 4 and catastrophic in season 12. Sampling the first and last transition is the coverage pattern the project already names as a defect, because the boundary that breaks is the one nobody sampled.
note: A rollover fault that changes ratings distribution or churn is a lifecycle question, not a scheduling one; hand it to the people lifecycle drift watch. Keep this loop on structural legality so a fix here cannot be justified by a distributional argument.

The run counts as complete only if it ends with the suite summary line; a non-zero exit with no summary is an abort, and an abort is reported as an abort rather than as a failure. title: College acquisition legality sweep
summary: Sweeps recruiting, the transfer portal, redshirts, commitments and scholarship limits for states the rules permit on paper but the code can reach illegally.
seoTitle: College Acquisition Legality Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Finds the illegal roster and eligibility states reachable through the college acquisition systems by asserting the rules module rather than the happy path.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Take one college acquisition rule that the rules module fixes and the suites do not enforce end to end: scholarship count, eligibility clock, redshirt legality, commitment uniqueness or portal window. Assert it after every transaction rather than at rest, then run the --college-commitments, --college-state, --redshirt-only, --portal-policy, --portal-transaction and --portal-scheduler suites. Fix the system, not the rule. Stop when two consecutive passes add a rule and find nothing. Escalate any rule the documents leave ambiguous.
verifyTitle: The rule holds after every transaction in the sweep, not only when the world is at rest.
verifyDetail: Assert immediately after each commitment, portal move, redshirt decision and scholarship award, because a system that reaches an illegal state and repairs it before the next week boundary still corrupts anything that read the state in between. Run the six college suites as a set. Express the assertion against the rules module constants so a rule change moves the check with it.
useWhen: Use after any change under the college systems, and whenever a rule stated in docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md sections 4.1, 4.3 or 11.1 is enforced at one call site rather than as an invariant. The portal has policy, matching, scheduling, transaction and contract suites, which is a strong sign that the rule surface is wide enough for a gap to hide in.
steps: List the college acquisition rules the rules module fixes as constants.
For each, find where it is enforced: at the call site, at a week boundary, or as an invariant.
Pick one enforced at a call site and promote it to a post-transaction invariant.
Run the six college suites as a set and record every illegal intermediate state.
Fix the system so the state is unreachable rather than repaired after the fact.
Re-run the set, then run --core-contracts to confirm nothing wider broke.
If a document leaves the rule ambiguous, amend canon first, then implement; never encode it only in code.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: The college tier is where the project put both of its unsolved risks, and acquisition is the part of it with the most transactions per week. Rules enforced at call sites are the classic source of unknown faults: every call site that exists is correct, and the fault is the call site added later that nobody remembered to guard. Promoting a rule to an invariant moves it from something a developer must remember to something the suite cannot avoid noticing.
note: An illegal state that only survives inside a single week advance is still a fault, because read models and the news feed can observe it. Do not accept before-next-boundary repair as a fix.

title: Pro front office legality sweep
summary: Holds the salary cap, contracts, the draft and the player market to invariants asserted after every transaction, including the dead-money overage the rules permit.
seoTitle: Pro Front Office Legality Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Hunts illegal cap, contract and roster states in the professional tier by asserting legality after each transaction rather than at the week boundary.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Take one professional rule the rules module fixes and the suites check only at rest: cap compliance including permitted dead-money overage, contract validity, roster limits, depth-chart completeness or draft order. Assert it after every transaction, then run the --cap-compliance, --pro-management, --pro-market, --pro-draft-probe and --depth-chart suites. Fix the system, never the limit. Money stays integer dollars. Stop when two consecutive passes add a rule and find nothing. Escalate any ambiguity to canon before coding it.
verifyTitle: Every professional team is legal after every transaction, with overage attributable only to dead money.
verifyDetail: Run the five professional suites as a set after each change. Cap legality must hold for every team at every point the sweep observes, and any overage must be traceable to dead money rather than tolerated as slack. Confirm no currency value is held or computed as floating point, since docs and CLAUDE.md fix money as integer dollars and a rounding fault in a cap check reads as a rules bug.
useWhen: Use after any change to the cap system, contracts, the draft, free agency or the depth chart, and whenever a professional rule is enforced at a call site rather than as an invariant. The prior build's cap system needed practice-squad defences, which is recorded as knowledge worth keeping rather than a solved problem.
steps: List the professional rules the rules module fixes and where each is enforced.
Pick one checked only at rest and promote it to a post-transaction invariant.
Assert permitted overage as attributable rather than as a tolerance.
Run the five professional suites as a set and record illegal intermediate states.
Fix the system so the state is unreachable; do not raise a limit to accommodate it.
Scan the touched paths for floating-point currency and remove any found.
Re-run the set plus --core-contracts.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: Cap systems fail in the direction of permissiveness, because every individual transaction looks affordable and the illegality is a property of the sequence. That makes at-rest checking structurally unable to find the interesting faults: by the time the world is at rest, the system has usually already repaired itself, and the corruption is in whatever read the state mid-sequence. Attributing overage rather than tolerating it is what turns a soft limit back into a hard one.
note: A cap repair that changes how teams behave in the market is a design change and belongs in canon before code. Keep the repair to legality and hand behavioural consequences to the owner.

title: People lifecycle drift watch
summary: Watches ratings, ages, injuries, discipline and tenure across long runs for distributional drift the per-week suites cannot see.
seoTitle: People Lifecycle Drift Watch | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Bands the distributions that progression, decline, injury and turnover produce over many seasons, so a slow drift is caught as a failure rather than accepted as the world.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Pick one lifecycle distribution with no band: rating spread by tier, age curve, injury incidence and duration, discipline frequency, tenure length or churn rate. State a band with its source, assert it at several season indices across a long run, then run the --people-lifecycle, --discipline, --roster-tenure, --injury-evidence and --programme-evolution suites. Fix the model when the band breaks. Stop when two consecutive passes add a band and find nothing. Ask before amending a decline age or trait constant.
verifyTitle: Each banded distribution holds at every sampled season index, not only at the start and the end.
verifyDetail: Sample at several season indices across the run, because a drift that is monotone shows only in the middle if the endpoints happen to agree. State each band's source: a document section, a research figure, or an explicitly recorded assumption. A band with no source is a guess presented as a threshold, which is the fault this loop exists to prevent rather than create.
useWhen: Use when a lifecycle behaviour is implemented but its long-run consequence is unbanded, after any change to progression, decline, injury or turnover, and whenever the soak's churn assertion is being relied on as a proxy for something more specific. Decline ages and traits are fixed in docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md sections 11.3.2 and 11.3.3, so the constants exist even where the resulting distributions are unchecked.
steps: List the lifecycle distributions the world produces and which have a stated band.
Pick one unbanded distribution whose drift would change the game most.
State a band and name its source explicitly; if there is no source, record it as an assumption.
Assert it at several season indices across a long run, not only at the endpoints.
Run the five lifecycle suites and record which index first breaks the band.
Fix the model. Never widen the band, and never move the sampled index to one that passes.
Amend canon first if the fix implies a change to a documented constant.
Record the band and its source in docs/STATUS.md; repeat until two consecutive passes are clean.
why: Drift is the fault class that per-week testing cannot detect by construction: every individual step is legal and the world is still wrong ten seasons later. The soak asserts that churn stays in band, which is a partial proxy the documents already describe as partial. Turning specific distributions into specific bands is what converts a vague sense that the league feels off into a failing assertion with a season index attached.
note: Do not invent a band from a plausible-sounding number. If no source exists, record it as an explicitly stated assumption with its reasoning, so the next reader can argue with it rather than inherit it as fact.

title: Career arc continuity hunt
summary: Walks a coach career from the college game through promotion into the pro league, asserting that identity, history and stakes survive every transition.
seoTitle: Career Arc Continuity Hunt | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Hunts the continuity faults in the promotion arc by walking a full career and asserting that no record, relationship or consequence is dropped at a tier boundary.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Walk one coach career across the college-to-pro promotion and assert that one carried thing survives intact: career record, coaching tree, rivalry history, job security state, staff relationships or archived seasons. Run the --career-arc, --career-control, --coaching-tree, --professional-career-session and --history-archive suites. Fix the transition where something is dropped or duplicated. Stop when two consecutive passes add a carried thing and find nothing. Ask before changing what the promotion arc carries.
verifyTitle: Every asserted carried record is present, unduplicated and correctly attributed on both sides of the promotion.
verifyDetail: Assert on both sides of the boundary and after an archive cycle, since a record can survive promotion and be lost at the next season archive. Run --history-archive and --m7-gate alongside the career suites so archive accounting is checked in the same pass. Duplication counts as a failure: a doubled career record is as wrong as a missing one and is easier to miss.
useWhen: Use when the promotion arc must preserve continuity, which docs/02-GAME-DESIGN.md section 9 requires as a v1 feature rather than a sequel. Use after any change to career state, the coaching tree, job security or history archiving.
steps: List what the promotion arc is documented to carry from the college tier into the pro league.
Pick one carried thing that no assertion checks across the boundary.
Walk a career to the promotion and assert its presence, count and attribution on both sides.
Run the career suites plus --history-archive and --m7-gate.
Fix the transition where a record is dropped, duplicated or misattributed.
Re-run and confirm the record also survives a subsequent archive cycle.
Record the widening in docs/STATUS.md and repeat.
Stop after two consecutive clean passes, or when what should carry is a design question.
why: The promotion is the single moment in the game where the player's whole history changes hands between two systems, and it happens once per career, which is exactly the frequency at which faults go unnoticed. A dropped rivalry or a duplicated record does not crash anything; it quietly makes the career the player has been building mean less. Continuity is only testable by walking the boundary, because no static check can tell that something should have been carried.
note: If the documents do not say whether something carries, that is a design question for canon and the owner, not a default to pick. Record it and stop rather than deciding it in code.

title: Architecture boundary scan widening
summary: Rewrites each boundary scan to enumerate its class by construction, so a new file, symbol or import is covered the day it is added rather than the day someone remembers it.
seoTitle: Architecture Boundary Scan Widening | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Converts hand-listed source scans into constructed enumerations across the engine/UI boundary, the hashValue ban and the composition layer's file-level rule.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Take one source scan in the contract suite and check whether it enumerates its class by construction or spot-checks a hand-written list. Rewrite one hand-listed scan per pass to enumerate from the file system or the type graph, then run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane core. Fix every violation the wider scan finds. Stop when two consecutive passes widen a scan and find nothing. Ask before exempting any file from a boundary rule.
verifyTitle: Each rewritten scan fails when a violating file is added, without that file being listed anywhere.
verifyDetail: Prove the widening by adding a deliberately violating file, confirming the scan fails, then removing it. A scan that passes both before and after has not been widened. Run --core-contracts after each rewrite. The rules to hold are zero SwiftUI imports under FootballSimCore, no seed derived from hashValue, no GameState named in the UI target, and inside the composition layer the same rule file by file rather than module by module.
useWhen: Use whenever a boundary is enforced by a scan, and especially where the scan reads as a list of known files. The project's own convention names this as a defect: the coverage boundary must not become the quality boundary, and spot-check tests over hand-listed instances are not coverage. A chrome-attachment sweep was already made exhaustive for exactly this reason, because the failure mode is silent rather than a compile error.
steps: List every source scan in the contract suite and classify each as constructed or hand-listed.
Pick the hand-listed scan guarding the most consequential rule.
Rewrite it to enumerate its class from the file system or the type graph.
Add a deliberately violating file and confirm the scan now fails.
Remove the violating file and run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane core.
Fix every real violation the wider scan surfaced; do not add an exemption list.
If an exemption is genuinely required, escalate it rather than encoding it.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: A silent boundary rule is the most dangerous kind, because nothing fails until the architecture has already eroded. Hand-listed scans encode the moment they were written and decay from then on; every file added afterwards is outside the check and nobody notices, since the suite is green. Widening by construction is the only change that makes the scan cover work that has not been written yet, which is where the unknown faults necessarily are.
note: An exemption list is a coverage boundary wearing a disguise. If one seems unavoidable, that is a design question for docs/03b-ARCHITECTURE.md and the owner, not a line to add inside the test.

title: Save durability hunt
summary: Attacks the save format with hostile and truncated inputs and every schema boundary, so corruption is refused with a plain message rather than partially opened.
seoTitle: Save Durability Hunt | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Hunts the persistence faults that only appear on a malformed, truncated, older or newer save by constructing the hostile input rather than waiting for one.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Construct one hostile save the suite does not currently cover: truncated envelope, corrupted entity key, invalid calendar, malformed history ledger, an older schema version or a newer one. Assert it is refused or migrated with a plain message and no partial open, then run the --save-document, --history-archive and --core-contracts suites. Fix the decode path, never the assertion. Stop when two consecutive passes add a hostile input and find nothing. Ask before changing the save schema version.
verifyTitle: Every hostile input is refused or migrated cleanly, with whole-root integrity re-checked on decode.
verifyDetail: A newer-schema save must be refused with a plain message rather than partially opened, and a corrupted one must reach the recovery path rather than a crash. Whole-root integrity is enforced again when a save root decodes, so assert that the integrity check actually ran rather than that the decode returned. Run --save-document with --history-archive so ledger and archive accounting are attacked in the same pass.
useWhen: Use after any change to the save envelope, the schema version, entity stores or the history ledger, and before any release, since the pre-deployment checklist requires migration fixtures at every schema version boundary and a corrupted-save recovery path exercised. Save writes must never happen on the main actor, which is a separate assertion in the same lane.
steps: List the save failure modes the suite constructs today.
List the ones a real device can produce and the suite does not: truncation, partial write, version skew, key mismatch.
Construct one uncovered hostile input as a fixture.
Assert the refusal, migration or recovery behaviour, including that the message is plain rather than technical.
Run --save-document, --history-archive and --core-contracts.
Fix the decode or migration path so the bad input cannot partially apply.
Confirm the write path is still off the main actor and inside the write budget.
Record the fixture and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: Persistence faults are the only ones in this project that destroy something the player cannot get back, which is why the rubric classes data loss as P0 and stops. They are also the faults least likely to be found by ordinary play, because the hostile input arrives once, on someone else's device, after a crash nobody reproduced. Constructing the hostile input is the only way to look; waiting for one is how the previous build learned its save was 8.3 MB.
note: A partially applied migration is worse than a refused save. If a fix cannot make a migration atomic, refuse the save and say so plainly rather than opening it halfway.

title: Soak horizon extension
summary: Extends the long-run soak one assertion or one horizon at a time and treats every unbounded collection as a defect rather than a growth curve.
seoTitle: Soak Horizon Extension | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Grows what the twenty-season soak asserts and how far it runs, so slow corruption and unbounded growth surface as failures instead of as save size.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Add one assertion to the soak that docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 6 requires and it does not yet make, or extend the horizon past twenty seasons at shipping league size. Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane soaks and the --m3-soak suite. Every collection that grows across seasons must be verified bounded by growth check, not by inspection. Fix the engine when an assertion breaks. Stop when two consecutive passes add an assertion and find nothing. Ask before reducing league size to make a run fit.
verifyTitle: The soak completes at shipping league size with the new assertion holding and save size under the eight megabyte ceiling.
verifyDetail: Run at shipping scale, since a soak at reduced league size proves something about a game nobody ships. Verify bounded collections by measuring growth across the run rather than by reading the bound in the code. Record the final save size against the four megabyte target and the eight megabyte hard ceiling. A soak that passes because it was shortened has not passed.
useWhen: Use before any release and after any change that adds a collection, an event kind or a per-season record. The prior build's unbounded free-agent pools and news feeds took saves to 8.3 megabytes, and bounding them brought it to 2.3, so this is a fault class with a worked example rather than a hypothetical.
steps: List what docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 6 says the soak asserts, and what it actually asserts.
Pick the largest gap, or extend the horizon if the assertion set is complete.
Add the assertion at shipping league size, not at a reduced one.
Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane soaks and --m3-soak.
For each collection that grew, prove the bound by growth measurement rather than by reading the code.
Fix the engine where an assertion breaks; never shorten the run or shrink the league to pass.
Record the final save size against the target and the ceiling.
Repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes, or when the run no longer completes in the available time.
why: Long-horizon faults are the definition of unknown: nothing about a single season shows them, and nobody plays twenty seasons before shipping. The soak is the only instrument that compresses that timeline, so every assertion missing from it is a fault class with no detector at all. Extending it is strictly additive to what the project can see, and the growth check specifically is what turns a stated bound into a verified one.
note: If the soak cannot complete in the available time, that is a finding to record, not a reason to reduce league size. Reducing programme count is D14's documented fallback for a performance ceiling and is an owner decision, not a test-runtime convenience.

companion.title: Soak run
companion.prompt: Run only what this prompt names, on the commit named in the request, built with -c release. Do not widen an assertion, tighten a band, adjust a budget or fix anything: this pass reports. Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane soaks and the --m3-soak suite at shipping league size, and the --m7-gate history lane if the request names it. Report every assertion's result, the save size at each checkpoint against the 8 MB ceiling, and the growth curve of every collection that grows across seasons. A collection reported as bounded by inspection rather than by a growth check is reported as unbounded. Do not reduce league size or shorten the horizon to make a run fit; if it will not fit, report that instead. The run counts as complete only if it ends with the suite summary line; a non-zero exit with no summary is an abort, and an abort is reported as an abort rather than as a failure. The soaks run for tens of minutes and the history lane for up to about an hour and a half: start it detached and never read a long silence as a hang. If there is no Swift toolchain, stop and report blocked.
companion.expect: expect 40 min to 1.5 h; the history lane is the long end

title: Performance budget potency
summary: Turns the week-advance probe from printed evidence into a gate that can fail, and rebuilds the season-length instrument that was deleted rather than implemented.
seoTitle: Performance Budget Potency | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Replaces an evidence-only performance probe with a threshold assertion, and restores the agency budget commitment that was removed from the gate table instead of being backed by a runner.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: PerformanceBudgetTests now has a runner and cannot fail: it asserts only the league size and that recruiting produced decisions, then prints PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE ONLY with no pass/fail threshold while week advance measures over the 2.0 s ceiling. Give one budget from the docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 7 table a real threshold assertion per pass, starting with week advance at shipping league size, and prove the assertion is potent by making it fail on a deliberate regression before you rely on it. AgencyBudgetTests was deleted rather than implemented and its commitment now sits in PRODUCT.md's unverified-targets table; rebuild the instrument and move the row back rather than leaving the promise unbacked. Report the measurement and the hardware, and keep host figures labelled as host figures: the device gate stays open and is not yours to close. Stop when every budget in the table has a runner, a figure and a threshold. Never report an estimate as a measurement, and never lower a ceiling to fit a measurement.
verifyTitle: Each budget's runner fails on a deliberate regression and passes without one, with the figure and the hardware recorded.
verifyDetail: Run the budget's command on a warmed Release build and record the figure, the target, the hard ceiling and the host. Then prove the gate is potent: introduce a deliberate regression past the ceiling, confirm the command goes red, remove it and confirm it goes green. A run that prints a number and passes regardless is evidence, not a gate, and must not be reported as one. Host figures never satisfy the device budgets in PRODUCT.md; those stay open until the owner measures them on the ratified hardware.
useWhen: Use when a performance commitment names an instrument that exists but asserts nothing, or when a budget in docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 7 has no figure at shipping league size. The failure this loop exists for is already in the tree: the week-advance runner was added, the commitment row was moved out of PRODUCT.md's gate table, CommitmentCoverageTest went green, and the budget is still missed.
steps: List every budget in docs/03-MATCH-ENGINE.md section 7 and the runner, figure and threshold each currently has.
Pick the budget whose absence of a threshold hides the largest measured miss; today that is week advance.
Add the threshold assertion against the documented ceiling, never against the last measurement.
Prove potency: regress the path deliberately, confirm red, remove the regression, confirm green.
Run the command on a warmed Release build and record figure, target, ceiling and host.
Rebuild the deleted agency instrument and move its commitment back into PRODUCT.md's gate table.
Re-run --catalog and --commitment-coverage so the table and the catalog agree.
Repeat for the next budget; stop when every row has a runner, a figure and a threshold.
why: A gate that cannot fail is worse than a missing one, because a missing gate is visible in the catalog and a vacuous gate reads as coverage. The performance runner was added in good faith and closed the registered-with-no-runner finding, but the property it claims to protect is not asserted anywhere, so the lane is green while week advance sits above its own hard ceiling. Restoring the deleted agency instrument matters for the same reason in the other direction: a commitment moved out of the gate table to make a test pass is standing rule 2 violated, and the promise survives the gate that was supposed to prove it.
note: Timing is hardware-dependent and this project's budgets are written against a physical iPhone 15 baseline. An agent may make the host figure real and the gate potent; it may not close the device gate. Record host measurements as host measurements and leave the device box for the owner.

companion.title: Budget measurement run
companion.prompt: Run only what this prompt names, on the commit named in the request, built with -c release. Do not widen an assertion, tighten a band, adjust a budget or fix anything: this pass reports. Run each performance budget command on a warmed build, three times, discarding no result. Report every figure with its target and its hard ceiling, and the host: model, core count, memory and operating system. Say explicitly for each whether the command asserted the threshold or merely printed the figure, because a printed figure is evidence and an asserted threshold is a gate. Host figures are host figures and never close a device budget. The run counts as complete only if it ends with the suite summary line; a non-zero exit with no summary is an abort, and an abort is reported as an abort rather than as a failure. A release build plus the lane itself runs long: start it detached and never read a long silence as a hang. If there is no Swift toolchain, stop and report blocked.
companion.expect: expect 20-40 min, most of it the release build

title: Accessibility matrix widening
summary: Grows the accessibility contract across the full screen inventory by construction, so a surface added today is checked at AX5 and under Reduce Motion today.
seoTitle: Accessibility Matrix Widening | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Extends contrast, type, motion, VoiceOver, touch-target and orientation checks to enumerate every screen family rather than a sampled set.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Take one accessibility check and confirm it enumerates all 62 screen families by construction rather than a sampled list. Widen one check per pass, then run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane accessibility. Fix every surface the wider check fails, at the supported layout floor and at AX5, in both appearances and both sensor orientations. Stop when two consecutive passes widen a check and find nothing. Ask before exempting a surface from the contract.
verifyTitle: Each widened check covers every registered screen family and fails when a new non-conforming surface is added.
verifyDetail: Prove the widening by adding a non-conforming surface, confirming the check fails, then removing it. Run --design-contracts, --reduce-motion and --screen-read-models together. The matrix is the supported layout floor of 844 by 390, both appearances, default and AX5 type, and sensor-left and sensor-right safe-area ownership. A check that passes on a sampled subset is a spot check, which the project classes as a defect rather than coverage.
useWhen: Use after adding or changing any surface, and whenever an accessibility check reads as a list of screens. Landscape-only means safe-area ownership differs by sensor side, which is a whole axis of the matrix that portrait designs never have to think about.
steps: List the accessibility checks in the design-contract suite and classify each as constructed or sampled.
Pick the sampled check guarding the most consequential promise.
Rewrite it to enumerate every registered screen family from the registry.
Add a deliberately non-conforming surface and confirm the check fails.
Remove it and run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane accessibility.
Fix every real failure at the layout floor, at AX5, in both appearances and both sensor orientations.
Confirm the coverage meta-assertion still holds, so the widening cannot silently narrow later.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: Accessibility regressions are added, not written: nobody makes a screen inaccessible on purpose, and the defect arrives with the next surface somebody built while the suite was green. That makes constructed enumeration the entire mechanism, because it is the only form of the check that covers a screen written after the check was. Three accessibility premises in this project are also recorded as unverified against the human interface guidelines, so widening the matrix is what turns a cited-from-memory rule into an enforced one.
note: Simulator and device confirmation is an owner action. An agent may widen the checks and fix what they catch, and must not report a visual walkthrough it did not perform. The touch-target floor, Reduce Motion semantics and the TimelineView suppression API are all recorded as unverified premises; confirm them against the guidelines before hardening a check that depends on one.

title: Design token discipline sweep
summary: Holds every view to the design system by scanning for literals, unregistered symbols and unnamed motion across the whole view layer rather than a sampled part of it.
seoTitle: Design Token Discipline Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Widens the token, symbol and motion scans so a spacing, colour, radius, font size, symbol or animation added outside the system fails the build.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Pick one design-system rule enforced by a scan: token literals, the symbol register, or the motion register. Confirm the scan enumerates the whole view layer by construction, widen it if not, then run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane accessibility and the --core-contracts suite. Replace every literal the wider scan finds with its token; never add an exemption. Stop when two consecutive passes widen a scan and find nothing. Ask before adding a token, symbol or motion to the registry.
verifyTitle: Each scan covers every file in the view layer and fails when a literal or unregistered symbol is introduced.
verifyDetail: Prove the widening by introducing a literal and an unregistered symbol, confirming both fail, then removing them. Run --core-contracts and --design-contracts. A design-token literal in a view is a defect by project convention, so the scan finding one is the scan working, and the fix is the token rather than the exemption.
useWhen: Use after any view work and whenever a scan appears to cover a directory rather than a class. The registries are the single source for spacing, radii, colours, font sizes, symbols and named motion, and a registry is only as strong as the scan that makes it mandatory.
steps: List the design-system scans and what each enumerates.
Pick one that enumerates by directory or by list rather than by construction.
Widen it to cover every file in the view layer.
Introduce a literal and an unregistered symbol and confirm both fail.
Remove them and run --core-contracts and --design-contracts.
Replace every real finding with its registered token, symbol or named motion.
If something genuinely has no token, amend the design system document first, then add it.
Record the widening and repeat; stop after two consecutive clean passes.
why: Visual drift is cumulative and individually invisible: one hard-coded spacing looks fine, and forty of them are a different product. The scan is the only thing that keeps the registry authoritative rather than aspirational, and a scan that covers a directory silently stops covering the files added outside it. Widening by construction is what makes the design system a constraint on future work instead of a description of past work.
note: Adding to a registry is a design decision and belongs in docs/04-UX-AND-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md before it appears in code, per the doc-first amendment rule. A scan exemption is never the right fix; it converts a caught defect into a permanent one.

title: Surface truthfulness audit
summary: Audits screens against the eight-dimension rubric one family at a time, treating any displayed fact without a read model as a defect rather than a placeholder.
seoTitle: Surface Truthfulness Audit | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Walks the screen inventory checking that every visible fact maps to a real read model, every family is reachable, and each surface clears the rubric gate.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Take one screen family and map every displayed fact to a named read model. Anything with no source is a truthfulness defect, not a placeholder. Score the family on all eight dimensions of docs/04b-AUDIT-RUBRIC.md and run the --screen-read-models, --history-read-model and --core-contracts suites. Fix P0 and P1 findings before anything else, and classify borderline findings upward. Stop when a family reaches 31 of 40 with no P0 or P1. Ask before inventing any figure the engine does not produce.
verifyTitle: Every displayed fact maps to a named read model and the family scores at least 31 of 40 with zero P0 or P1.
verifyDetail: The gate is 31 of 40 across eight dimensions with no P0 or P1 and no automatic design-specificity rejection. Run --screen-read-models and --core-contracts so reachability and error-surface assertions run in the same pass; an unreachable screen and a captured-but-unpresented error are both defects the suite can own. A production screen never carries a reference-data label, so a fixture left visible is itself a finding.
useWhen: Use on any surface before calling it production-grade, and on any family whose interior was built as chrome without its content. A prior adversarial review recorded 23 findings from four surfaces sampled of 62, and one open finding covers roughly 59 surfaces that remain chrome-only, so the population of unaudited families is large and known.
steps: Pick one screen family, preferring one never audited.
Enumerate every fact it displays and name the read model behind each.
Record any fact with no source as a truthfulness defect at the appropriate severity.
Score all eight dimensions against the anchors and classify borderline findings upward.
Run --screen-read-models, --history-read-model and --core-contracts.
Fix P0 and P1 findings first; a P0 stops the pass entirely.
Where a fact has no engine source, stop rather than deriving one, and record what the engine would need to produce it.
Record the score and findings, then take the next family; stop when the family clears the gate.
why: Dimension seven asks whether every displayed fact maps to a real read model, and it is the dimension a beautiful screen fails most quietly. A number that looks plausible and comes from nowhere is indistinguishable from a real one at a glance, survives review, and becomes a lie the product tells every time it renders. The project has already hit this exactly: a rating-uncertainty finding could not be closed because no scouting-confidence model exists and deriving one would print invented figures as fact.
note: Never invent a figure to fill a surface. If the engine cannot produce it, that is engine work or a design change, and both belong to canon and the owner. Simulator confirmation and the owner review questions in section 7 of the rubric are owner actions; a numeric score cannot overrule the owner on the fantasy and application-furniture questions.

title: Release gate traceability loop
summary: Keeps every commitment, registered gate, dispatched runner and status claim in agreement, so no promise is backed by a test that cannot run.
seoTitle: Release Gate Traceability Loop | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Closes the loop between the commitment table, the gate registry, the dispatched runners and the honest status document, one unbacked claim at a time.
author: Pro Football Coach project
prompt: Run the --catalog and --commitment-coverage suites and list every gate registered without a runnable command and every commitment naming one. Then check the other direction, which is how this gate was last made green: a commitment moved out of PRODUCT.md's gate table into the unverified-targets table makes the test pass without building anything, and standing rule 2 forbids it. Any row that moved needs its instrument built and the row moved back, or an owner decision to drop the promise. Close one gap per pass, then reconcile docs/STATUS.md so nothing unverified is described as verified. Stop when the catalog prints no missing runner, no commitment sits in the unverified table for want of an instrument, and status matches the tree. Ask before removing any commitment.
verifyTitle: The catalog prints a runner for every registered gate and the commitment coverage suite passes.
verifyDetail: --catalog prints MISSING RUNNER for any gate whose runner is nil, and --commitment-coverage asserts both that every commitment names a registered gate with a runnable command and that every registered gate declares its runner state. Both must be clean on the same commit. Then read docs/STATUS.md against the tree and confirm no file claims a build or a test run that did not happen.
useWhen: Use before any release and after any change to PRODUCT.md, SuiteCatalog or the dispatched commands. Four gates are currently registered with nil runners: agency budget, performance budget, two-tier consistency and smallest-device layout, and three of those are named in the commitment table, so the coverage assertions should be failing on them today.
steps: Run --catalog and record every gate printed as MISSING RUNNER.
Run --commitment-coverage and record every failing identifier.
Pick one gap. Build and dispatch the runner, or remove the commitment if the project no longer makes it.
Removing a commitment is an owner decision; propose it and stop rather than deleting the row.
Re-run --catalog and --commitment-coverage on the same commit.
Reconcile docs/STATUS.md: name every unverified thing as unverified, with its files.
Confirm no document in the repository claims a build or test run that did not happen.
Repeat until the catalog is clean and status matches the tree.
why: This is the loop that keeps every other loop honest. A commitment table is a coverage claim, and when a row names a gate that cannot run, the project is asserting a guarantee nobody holds, which is exactly how the previous build shipped a phase that had never been compiled. The fault class is invisible from inside any single suite because each suite passes; only the traceability check across the table, the registry and the dispatch sees it.
note: Never close a gap by deleting the assertion or the commitment on your own authority. The honest intermediate state is a recorded, named gap, which the pre-deployment checklist already treats as a stop rather than a warning. If there is no Swift toolchain, this loop stops as blocked; do not infer the suites' results by reading them.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: End-to-end journey walk
summary: Walks one mandatory acceptance journey end to end with a save and reload at every mutation, so a dead end between two green units is found before a player reaches it.
seoTitle: End-to-End Journey Walk | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Drives one of the eight acceptance journeys through the real app-layer entry points with interruption and reload at every boundary, because unit gates pass on the parts and journeys fail in the seams.
prompt: Take one journey from the acceptance set in docs/BETA-READINESS-CONSOLIDATED.md section 7, E2E-A through E2E-H, and walk it end to end as a headless integration test through the app-layer entry points rather than by calling the engine directly. Save and reload at every mutation boundary and assert that the destination, the pending task and the unapplied decision all survive the round trip. A dead end, a silently auto-skipped decision, a decision applied twice, or a control that cannot be reached from the previous step is a defect, not an unfinished screen. Run the --core-contracts and --screen-read-models suites. Fix the flow, never the journey. Stop when two consecutive passes add a journey step and find nothing. Escalate anything that needs a canon decision about what the journey should do before you implement one.
verifyTitle: The journey runs from its first screen to its last with a reload at every mutation, and no step dead-ends, auto-skips or applies twice.
verifyDetail: The walk must go through the same entry points the app uses, because the seam between the app layer and the engine is exactly where a journey fault lives and a direct engine call steps over it. Interrupt and reload at every safe boundary rather than only at the end; a journey that completes in one process and loses its place on reload has failed. Assert the pending decision set before and after each reload, not just the final state, so a decision that is dropped and a decision that is applied twice are distinguishable.
useWhen: Use when every unit gate is green and nobody can say whether a career can actually be played from a fresh install to a promotion. The failure class is already recorded: the career session rejects promotion acceptance while the resolver clears college control on accept, so there is no playable professional session even though both halves pass their own tests.
why: Every other loop in this series widens an oracle over a part. A journey fault lives in none of the parts: each unit is correct, each gate is green, and the seam between them drops a decision or refuses a transition. No amount of widening a per-system assertion reaches it, because the missing assertion is about a sequence rather than a state. The eight journeys are already written down as mandatory tests; treating them as manual aspirations is what let a career dead end survive a green suite.
note: This loop needs the app layer, so it stops as blocked where there is no Swift toolchain. Write the walk to the same standard, record it in docs/STATUS.md as unverified and never compiled, and never report a journey as walked because the code that walks it was written.
steps: Read the journey's definition and list every step, mutation and safe interruption boundary it names.
Map each step to the app-layer entry point that performs it, not to the engine call underneath.
Write the walk so it saves and reloads at every mutation boundary, asserting pending state across the round trip.
Run it, and run --core-contracts and --screen-read-models alongside it.
Classify each failure as dead end, auto-skip, double application or unreachable control before fixing anything.
Fix the flow; never adjust the journey to match what the code happens to do.
Record the journey's status in docs/STATUS.md, naming which steps are covered and which are not.
Repeat with the next journey; stop after two consecutive passes that add steps and find nothing.
