companion.prompt: Run only the twenty-plus season durability journey, E2E-H, on the commit named in the request, built with -c release. Expect tens of minutes; run it detached and do not read a long silence as a hang. At each season checkpoint report save size, load and write time, deterministic reload equality, bounded-collection growth and whether every screen family is still operable. Do not widen an assertion, tighten a budget or fix anything: report only. The run counts as complete only if it ends with the suite summary line; a non-zero exit with no summary is an abort to be reported as an abort, not as a failure. If there is no Swift toolchain, stop and report blocked.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: Dead control sweep
summary: Traces every enabled control to a real state change, so a control that acts on nothing, or only on debug text, is caught as a defect rather than passing as an unfinished screen.
seoTitle: Dead Control Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Enumerates the view layer's interactive controls by construction and follows each one through intent, authority, receipt, save and downstream consumer, treating an inert or lying control as a functional defect.
prompt: Enumerate every interactive control in the view layer by construction from the source rather than from a hand-written list. Take one screen family per pass and trace each enabled control through intent, authority, receipt, save and downstream consumer. Four things are defects, not placeholders: a control wired to an empty closure, a control disabled with no reason shown to the player, a control enabled while a known mandatory decision already makes it invalid so the rejection only arrives after the tap, and a control that mutates debug status text and never alters the live game. Run the --core-contracts and --screen-read-models suites. Fix the control or remove it; never leave an enabled control that cannot act. Stop when two consecutive passes add a family and find nothing. Ask before removing a control that canon names.
verifyTitle: Every enabled control in the family reaches a persisted state change, and every disabled one shows the player its reason.
verifyDetail: The enumeration is the whole of the check: a sweep over a hand-listed set of controls stops covering the layer the day a screen is added, which is this project's stated coverage-boundary defect. Derive the control set from the source or the type graph so a new control is swept the day it lands. For each control, the trace must end at a consumer that reads the change back, not at the store that accepted it; a receipt nothing reads is the same defect one step later.
useWhen: Use before any claim that a screen family is complete, and after adding any control. Ten inert or misleading controls are already recorded: inspect and delegate wired to empty closures, disabled roster routes, match-day controls that only move debug text, and continue buttons that stay enabled while a mandatory decision is known to block them.
why: The truthfulness audit asks whether a displayed fact has a read model. This is its dual and a different fault class: the control is displayed, the fact behind it is real, and pressing it does nothing. Neither a read-model check nor an accessibility check can see it, because the control has a label, a target and a size; what it lacks is an effect. A player finds this fault in the first minute and reads it as a broken game rather than an unfinished one.
note: Removing a control is a product change. Where canon names a control that has no implementation, the loop's job is to report the gap, not to delete the promise or invent the behaviour; that is a decision for the owner and, if it is a gameplay decision, for the documents first.
steps: Derive the full set of interactive controls in the view layer from the source, by construction.
Pick one screen family and list its controls with their enabled and disabled conditions.
Trace each enabled control through intent, authority, receipt, save and the consumer that reads it back.
Classify each finding as inert, unexplained-disabled, knowably-invalid-but-enabled, or debug-only.
Fix the control so it acts, or disable it with a reason the player can read.
Run --core-contracts and --screen-read-models and confirm the family is clean.
Record the family and its findings in docs/STATUS.md.
Repeat with the next family; stop after two consecutive clean passes.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: Gate potency sweep
summary: Proves each release gate can fail by feeding it a deliberate violation, so a suite that is green because it asserts nothing is caught before anyone trusts it.
seoTitle: Gate Potency Sweep | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Tests the tests: introduces a deliberate violation of the property each registered gate claims and requires the gate to go red, so a vacuous assertion cannot pass as coverage.
prompt: Take one registered release gate and prove it can fail. Introduce a deliberate violation of the property it claims, run its command, and confirm it goes red; then remove the violation and confirm it goes green. A gate that passes both ways asserts nothing about its property and is a defect however green the lane is. Two are known vacuous today: PerformanceBudgetTests prints PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE ONLY with no pass/fail threshold, and the calibration lane validates TOST mechanics, seed separation and result counts without asserting that any band actually holds. A third pattern to look for is an assertion that compares a set to its own definition, which is an identity rather than an exhaustiveness check. Fix the gate to assert its property; never delete or relocate the commitment instead. Run --catalog and --commitment-coverage after each change. Record each gate as potent or vacuous. Stop when every registered gate has been shown potent. Ask before landing an assertion that would turn a lane red on main.
verifyTitle: The gate goes red on a deliberate violation of the property it claims and green once the violation is removed.
verifyDetail: Both halves are required. A gate that goes red is not thereby potent, because it may be failing on something other than the property under test; confirm the failure message names the property. A gate that goes green afterwards is not thereby correct, but a gate that stays green through the violation is definitively vacuous. Keep the violation in a scratch commit that is never pushed, and confirm the tree is clean before recording the result, so the proof cannot be mistaken for the fix.
useWhen: Use before trusting any lane's green, and always before a release decision that rests on one. The mechanism this loop exists to catch is already in the history: a red commitment-coverage gate was made green by moving three commitments out of PRODUCT.md's gate table into a prose unverified-targets table, so the test passed because the table it checks shrank.
why: Every other loop widens an oracle and trusts the harness underneath it. This one distrusts the harness. A vacuous gate is worse than an absent one: an absent gate is visible in the catalog and is a known gap, while a vacuous gate reports coverage it does not have and is counted in a release decision. Standing rule 2 forbids fixing the instrument instead of the system, and a gate that cannot fail is that rule already broken and no longer detectable from the outside. Proving potency by deliberate violation is the only check that distinguishes a passing gate from a silent one.
note: The deliberate violation is a temporary local change and must never be committed, pushed or left in the tree. If a gate cannot be made potent without turning a lane red on main, that is a real failure being uncovered, not a reason to soften the assertion; report it and ask before landing it.
steps: List every gate in the catalog with its command and the property its commitment claims.
Pick one and read its body to predict whether it can fail at all.
Introduce a deliberate, local violation of the claimed property.
Run the gate's command and confirm it goes red with a message naming the property.
Remove the violation, confirm green, and confirm the tree is clean.
Where the gate stayed green, add the missing assertion and repeat the proof.
Record the gate as potent or vacuous in docs/STATUS.md with the evidence.
Repeat until every registered gate has been proven potent.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: CI lane routing audit
summary: Holds every named lane and registered gate to being reachable from a scheduled job, so a gate that exists and only ever runs by hand cannot be counted as coverage.
seoTitle: CI Lane Routing Audit | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Reconciles the lanes the verification script accepts, the gates the catalog registers and the jobs continuous integration actually schedules, then routes one unrouted gate per pass.
prompt: List every lane scripts/verify.sh accepts, every gate SuiteCatalog registers with its lane and default-run membership, and every command the workflows actually invoke. A lane no workflow runs and a gate outside every scheduled lane are uncovered however green they are locally, and today the soaks, calibration, accessibility, archive, release and app lanes all exist and none is scheduled. Close one gap per pass by routing the gate into a job, respecting the 180-minute job ceiling and the runner cap: a long lane belongs on its own scheduled job, not bolted onto the default one. Confirm the job actually ran the suite by its printed summary line rather than by exit code alone. Stop when every registered gate is reachable from a scheduled job. Ask before adding a job that would exceed the runner budget.
verifyTitle: Every registered gate is named by a scheduled job, and each job's log ends with the suite summary line it was meant to produce.
verifyDetail: The reconciliation must be derived, not asserted by hand: read the lane list from the script, the gate list from the catalog and the invocations from the workflow files, and assert the three agree by construction so a gate added later is routed or reported the day it lands. Exit code alone is not evidence a lane ran: a full lane can abort mid-run, print nothing and leave an ordinary non-zero status, so the acceptance check is the summary line. Long lanes are queued against a small runner pool, so a pending check usually means queue depth rather than a defect.
useWhen: Use whenever a gate is added, a lane is added, or a release claim rests on a suite nobody has watched run in CI. The gap is live: continuous integration runs one job invoking the default lane, so the soaks that back the save-size commitment, the calibration lane and the app build are registered, runnable and never scheduled.
why: A gate has three separate ways to be absent: not written, written with no runner, and runnable but never run. The catalog loop closes the second. This one closes the third, which is the one that survives every other check, because from inside the repository a gate with a working command looks identical whether or not anything ever invokes it. Scheduling is the only thing that converts a command into coverage, and the budget for scheduling is finite, so the routing decision has to be made deliberately rather than inherited.
note: Runner time is a real constraint, not a formality: jobs are capped at 180 minutes against a small concurrent pool, and a soak or archive lane can consume most of one. Route long lanes to their own scheduled job on a cadence the owner has agreed rather than adding them to the job that gates every pull request.
steps: Read the accepted lane list out of scripts/verify.sh and the gate list out of the catalog.
Read what the workflow files actually invoke, and build the three-way reconciliation.
List every gate reachable from no scheduled job, and every lane no job runs.
Pick one and decide where it belongs: the pull-request job, or its own scheduled job.
Route it, respecting the job ceiling and the runner cap.
Confirm from the log that the suite ran to its summary line, not merely that the job exited zero.
Assert the reconciliation by construction so a later gate is routed or reported automatically.
Repeat until every registered gate is reachable from a scheduled job.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: Packaging and submission readiness
summary: Closes one submission requirement per pass and asserts the built bundle carries only intended files, so the archive is not discovered to be unshippable at upload time.
seoTitle: Packaging and Submission Readiness | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Adds the missing App Store submission resources one at a time and replaces bundle inspection with a machine-asserted allowlist, so packaging defects fail a lane rather than a review.
prompt: Take one thing the submission path requires that the repository does not yet have: the app icon set, the privacy manifest including the required-reason API declaration for the save loader's file-metadata reads, the export-compliance declaration, the version and build numbers, or explicit source and resource roots in App/project.yml in place of a bare whole-directory source list that packages build databases and compiler artefacts into the app. Add it, then assert it by construction rather than by inspection: a bundle allowlist check that fails when an unintended file is packaged, run from a clean checkout. Run ./scripts/verify.sh --lane app. Where a step is owner-only, such as choosing the product's export-compliance answer or the signed archive itself, prepare it and stop there. Stop when every box in the checklist's release-hygiene section is either machine-asserted or explicitly named as owner-only. Ask before choosing a product answer on the owner's behalf.
verifyTitle: The project generates and builds from a clean checkout, and the bundle allowlist check fails when an unintended file is packaged.
verifyDetail: Generate the project from a clean checkout rather than the working tree, because the defect being hunted is exactly the tree's incidental files reaching the bundle. Prove the allowlist is potent the way the potency loop does: add an unintended file, confirm the check goes red, remove it and confirm green. Inspection is not verification here; the existing simulator build was described as containing dozens of junk top-level resources while every suite was green, because nothing asserted the bundle's contents.
useWhen: Use before any archive, TestFlight upload or store submission, and after any change to the project specification. Three required resources are absent from the tree right now and none of them is a code change: there is no app icon set, no privacy manifest and no export-compliance declaration.
why: Every other loop protects the game. This one protects the ability to ship it, which fails in a completely different way: not a wrong result but a rejected upload, discovered at the last possible moment, when the fix is a resource nobody wrote. These are the cheapest items on the whole checklist and the ones most likely to be left because they are not interesting, and the bundle allowlist is the only one of them that can regress silently once fixed.
note: Export compliance is a product answer about the app, not a technical detail an agent may pick, and the signed archive and its upload are owner actions. Prepare the declaration and the evidence; never assert that an archive was built, installed or submitted.
steps: List the submission requirements and check each against the tree rather than against the documents.
Pick the missing item whose absence would stop an upload soonest.
Add it, and add the assertion that would catch its removal.
Replace the whole-directory source list with explicit source and resource roots.
Add a bundle allowlist check and prove it fails on an unintended file.
Generate and build from a clean checkout with ./scripts/verify.sh --lane app.
Record which remaining items are owner-only and what the owner needs from the agent to close them.
Repeat until every release-hygiene box is machine-asserted or named as owner-only.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: Branch integration convergence
summary: Converges divergent agent branches onto one immutable candidate, so a gate is proven on the tree that will ship rather than on a tree nobody will ever build.
seoTitle: Branch Integration Convergence | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Dispositions every unmerged branch as integrate, supersede or reject and folds the survivors into a single candidate commit, because a gate proven on a divergent branch proves nothing about the release.
prompt: Survey every unmerged branch and classify each as integrate, supersede or reject, recording the reason. Integrate one per pass onto a single candidate, run the default lane on the result, and root-cause any red rather than re-pinning a fingerprint or re-recording a literal to match. Look for duplicate work before integrating: two agents have already built the same gate twice, and the branch whose version landed was not the branch that built it first, so check whether the work in front of you already exists on the trunk in another form. A red suite on the trunk is usually an unmerged fix rather than a new defect, so look for one before debugging. Watch for a branch that closed a finding by moving the promise instead of building the instrument; that is standing rule 2 broken and it integrates as a defect, not as a fix. Stop when every branch is dispositioned and one commit carries the whole candidate. Ask before rejecting a branch that carries unique work.
verifyTitle: Every unmerged branch is dispositioned with a reason, and one commit carries the candidate with the default lane green on it.
verifyDetail: The candidate must be a single immutable commit, not a working tree: a review of a tree that is still being edited cannot be reproduced, and a build whose inputs changed during compilation is not evidence. Run the lane on the integrated commit rather than trusting per-branch results, because branch-era pass counts describe code that no longer exists in that combination. A branch recorded as superseded needs the commit that supersedes it named, so the disposition can be checked later rather than believed.
useWhen: Use before any release decision, and whenever agent branches have accumulated faster than they have merged. The condition is chronic here rather than occasional: dozens of unmerged branches exist, and the branch carrying this loop series was itself hundreds of commits behind the trunk, which is how three of its loops came to open on premises that had already been closed.
why: Every gate in this project is proven against a commit. If no single commit carries the whole candidate, every green result describes a tree that will never be built, and the release decision rests on a combination nobody has tested. Divergence also silently invalidates the loops themselves: a loop written against a stale trunk aims at a fault that has been fixed, or misses the worse fault the fix introduced. Convergence is therefore not tidying; it is the precondition that makes any other loop's result mean something.
note: Integration is where the temptation to re-pin is strongest, because a merge conflict in a fingerprint looks like bookkeeping. It is not: a fingerprint that changed on merge is either a real divergence or a re-key, and both need root-causing. Never resolve one by taking either side.
steps: List every unmerged branch with its divergence from the trunk and what it uniquely carries.
Classify each as integrate, supersede or reject, and record the reason and the superseding commit.
Check the trunk for the same work already landed in another form before integrating anything.
Integrate one branch onto the candidate and run the default lane on the result.
Root-cause every red; look for an unmerged fix before assuming a new defect.
Reject any change that closed a finding by moving a promise rather than building an instrument.
Record the candidate commit and its lane result in docs/STATUS.md.
Repeat until every branch is dispositioned and one commit carries the candidate.

author: Pro Football Coach project
title: Owner gate evidence pack
summary: Prepares the artefacts the owner-only checklist boxes need, without ever asserting a box an agent may not assert.
seoTitle: Owner Gate Evidence Pack | Pro Football Coach project loop
description: Builds the walkthrough scripts, device matrices, capture lists and measurement protocols that the owner-only release gates require, labelling every unobserved expectation as a prediction.
prompt: Take one owner-only box from the checklist's owner-gate section and prepare everything an agent legitimately can: the exact walkthrough steps with their expected results, the device and appearance matrix including the supported layout floor and the largest supported class, the capture list the evidence bundle must retain, or the protocols and instruments for the season-length timing decision and the first-session onboarding decision. Order the steps by how fast they fail, so a syntax error costs seconds rather than a whole lane. Label every expected result the agent has not observed as a prediction, never as a record, and state plainly what the pack cannot see: a headless suite cannot judge a rendered property such as clipping or reachability. Hand the pack to the owner and stop. Never report a walkthrough, a device measurement or a simulator demonstration as having happened. Stop when every owner-gate box has a runnable pack. Ask before changing what a protocol measures.
verifyTitle: Each owner-gate box has a pack the owner can run unaided, with predictions marked as predictions and the pack's blind spots stated.
verifyDetail: The acceptance check is that someone with the device and no context can run the pack start to finish without asking a question, which is what makes it evidence rather than a note. Every expected result must carry its provenance: observed by the agent, produced by a suite, or predicted. A pack that reads as a record of a session that never happened is the exact failure this project has already had, and it is worse than no pack, because the next reader has no way to tell which lines were real.
useWhen: Use when the machine gates are closing and the remaining boxes are ones no agent may assert: the simulator walkthrough, physical-device performance, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type at the largest accessibility size, Reduce Motion through a full match, the season-timing protocol and the onboarding protocol.
why: The owner-only boxes are the largest untouched block on the checklist and the series otherwise treats them as out of scope, which is correct about authority and wrong about effort: escalation is a statement of who decides, not a reason to hand over nothing. An owner with a device and no script will not run a ten-step accessibility matrix from memory, so the box stays open indefinitely. Preparing the pack is the whole of the agent's legitimate contribution, and it is most of the work.
note: This loop's single failure mode is writing the pack in the past tense. Predictions are predictions. If a suite backs a line, name the suite; if nothing does, say so. A pack that quietly reads as a record is how a phase that had never been compiled came to be reported as shipped.
steps: List the owner-only boxes and what each would need in order to be closed in one sitting.
Pick one and write its steps in the order that fails fastest.
State the device, appearance, orientation and accessibility-size matrix the box requires.
Give each step an expected result, labelled as observed, suite-produced or predicted.
State what the pack cannot see, especially rendered properties a headless suite cannot judge.
List the captures the evidence bundle must retain for the release commit.
Hand the pack over and record in docs/STATUS.md that the box remains open pending the owner.
Repeat until every owner-gate box has a pack; never mark one closed.
